references.text: Joshua answers the complaint of Joseph's sons about the hill country and iron chariots, and urges them to drive out the Canaanites despite their strength.
Judah could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley because they had iron chariots, the same challenge that Joseph's sons faced.
Sisera had nine hundred iron chariots, showing the military superiority of the Canaanites with iron chariots in the valleys.
Mentions Beth-shan and its daughter towns belonging to Manasseh, the same area referred to in this verse.
The Jezreel Valley is mentioned as part of Issachar's inheritance, the same valley referred to here.
The Jezreel Valley was where the Midianites and Amalekites camped, showing the strategic importance of the valley.
The Egyptians had iron chariots that were used against Israel, an example of the enemy's use of this technology.
